The Atlanta Hawks are an American professional basketball team based in Atlanta.
The Atlanta Hawks compete in the National Basketball Association (NBA) as a member of the Southeast Division of the Eastern Conference.
The Atlanta Hawks play their home games at State Farm Arena.
The origins of the Atlanta Hawks can be traced back to the Buffalo Bisons franchise, which was founded in 1946.
The Bisons were a member of the National Basketball League (NBL).
The team's first game – a 50–39 victory over the Syracuse Nationals – was played on November 8, 1946.
William "Pop" Gates and William "Dolly" King were one of the first two African-American players in the NBL.
On December 25, 1946, Leo Ferris announced that the team would be moving to Moline, Illinois.
Upon relocation to Moline, the team was renamed the Tri-Cities Blackhawks.
The team played their home games at Wharton Field House in Moline.
Leo Ferris and Ben Kerner owned the Tri-Cities Blackhawks.
In 1949, the Blackhawks became one of the National Basketball Association's 17 original teams after a merger between the NBL and BAA.
Bob Pettit was drafted by the Hawks in 1954.
The Hawks moved to St. Louis in 1955 and became the St. Louis Hawks.
In 1956, Bob Pettit captured the league's first official Most Valuable Player award.
The St. Louis Hawks drafted Bill Russell in the first round (second overall pick) in 1957.
They immediately traded Russell to the Boston Celtics for Cliff Hagan and Ed Macauley.
In 1958, the Hawks won their first NBA Championship after defeating the Boston Celtics in a double-overtime thriller in game seven.
Bob Pettit scored 50 points in the final game of the series that year.
The Hawks finished four games under .500 in 1957 but still won the division title and advanced to the Finals.
In 1968, Kerner sold the Hawks to Atlanta real estate developer Tom Cousins and former Georgia governor Carl Sanders.
While a new arena was being constructed, the team played at Alexander Memorial Coliseum on the campus of Georgia Tech for four seasons.
The Hawks debuted a new logo and colors in 1972.
Ted Turner bought the team in 1977 and hired Hubie Brown to become head coach.
In 1982, the franchise acquired superstar Dominique Wilkins.
From 1985 to 1989, the Hawks were among the league's elite, winning 50 games or more each season.
The Hawks drafted Stacey Augmon with their ninth overall pick in the 1991 NBA draft.
In 1993–94, the Hawks won 57 games and tied a team record.
In 1998, Dominique Wilkins was awarded the J. Walter Kennedy Citizenship Award for his charitable endeavors.
On March 6, 2015, Dominique Wilkins received a statue in front of Philips Arena.
Steve Smith helped lead Atlanta to three Semifinals appearances in the Eastern Conference during the mid-to-late 1990s.
At the beginning of the 1994–95 season, the Hawks traded forward Kevin Willis to the Miami Heat for Steve Smith and Grant Long.
Coach Wilkens broke the record (previously held by coach Red Auerbach) for most victories by an NBA head coach with victory number 939 in the 1994–95 season.
The Hawks finished fifth in the Central Division with a 42–40 record and were swept by the Indiana Pacers in the first round of the playoffs.
In 1997, the Hawks acquired Christian Laettner from the Minnesota Timberwolves; he would get an All-Star appearance in 1997.
The Hawks upset the third-seeded Pacers in the first round in five games but lost to the Orlando Magic in the semifinals.
The Omni was designed with weathering steel that was intended to rust into a seal around the arena so it could last for decades.
However, the designers and architects did not reckon on Atlanta's humid subtropical climate, causing the Omni to never stop rusting.
When Turner won an NHL franchise, the Atlanta Thrashers, one condition was that a new arena had to be in place before the new team took the ice for the first time.
Eventually, it was decided that The Omni would be demolished and a new arena for the Hawks and the expansion NHL Thrashers would be built on the same area.
The Hawks moved back to Georgia Tech's Alexander Memorial Coliseum after the 1997 playoffs until Philips Arena opened before the 1999–2000 season.
In the 1996–97 season, Dikembe Mutombo won defensive player of the year awards back-to-back.
The Hawks defeated the Detroit Pistons in five games in the first round of the 1997 NBA playoffs but lost to the defending champs Chicago Bulls in five games.
Game 4, an 89–80 loss, would be the last game at The Omni.
In 1997–98, forward Alan Henderson won Most Improved Player award.
The Hawks defeated the Pistons again in five games in the first round of the playoffs but were swept by the eighth-seeded New York Knicks in the second round.
In the 1999–2000 season, the Hawks traded Steve Smith to Portland for Isaiah Rider and Jim Jackson.
They also sent Mookie Blaylock and a first-round draft pick to the Golden State Warriors for Bimbo Coles and a first-round draft pick.
The Smith/Rider trade sent the Hawks into a downward spiral.
By contrast, Rider had a history of behavioral problems both on and off the court.
Rider missed the first day of training camp and was late for two games.

After reports that he smoked marijuana in an Orlando hotel room during a January road trip, the league demanded that he attend drug counseling, and fined him a total of $200,000 until he agreed to go.
When he showed up late for a March game, the Hawks released him.
The Hawks drafted Spanish star Pau Gasol third in 1999 but his rights were ceded to the Memphis Grizzlies in a trade involving Shareef Abdur-Rahim.
Abdur-Rahim became the team's scoring leader and made his only All-Star appearance in 2002.
The Hawks ended up 33–49 for the 2001–02 season.
In 2002, the Hawks sent Kukoc to the Milwaukee Bucks for All-Star Glenn Robinson.
Robinson led the team with 20.8 ppg but the Hawks still failed to make the playoffs for the 2002–03 season, finishing with a 35–47 record.
In February 2004, Rasheed Wallace played one game for the Hawks before being traded to the Detroit Pistons in a three-way trade involving Boston Celtics and Portland.
The Hawks ended their 2003–04 season with a 28–54 record.
In 2005, the Hawks acquired seven-time NBA All-Star Joe Johnson.
Despite their league-worst record the previous season, the Hawks only landed the number two pick in the 2005 NBA draft lottery.
With the second pick, the Hawks selected Marvin Williams of North Carolina.
In the 2006 draft, the Hawks selected former Duke star Shelden Williams with the fifth overall pick.
Hope and redemption appeared to be on the horizon for the Hawks beginning in 2007 when they selected Al Horford third in the NBA draft.
Horford nearly averaged a double-double during his rookie season and was the only unanimous selection to the All-Rookie First Team as well as being runner-up for Rookie of the Year honors.
The Hawks won their first season opener since 1998, defeating the Dallas Mavericks 101–94.
For the 2007–08 season, the Atlanta Hawks updated the logos and uniforms that saw navy blue become the primary color with red relegated to trim color status.
In 2008, the Hawks won 47 games, their first winning season since 1999.
Again they were pushed to a Game 7 in the first round but capitalized on home-court advantage earning their first playoff series win since 1999 against the Miami Heat.
The Hawks were swept by the Cleveland Cavaliers 4–0 in the Conference Semifinals.
In 2009, the Hawks improved further, winning 53 games, their first 50-win season since 1997–98.
Al Horford and Joe Johnson were named to the All-Star team for the first time since 1998.
The Hawks won a hard-fought seven-game series against the Milwaukee Bucks but were swept by the Orlando Magic in the second round, with every game a one-sided contest.
In mid-season, Mike Bibby was traded to the Washington Wizards for Kirk Hinrich.
The Hawks finished the season losing their final six games.
In the playoffs, the Hawks beat the Magic in six games but subsequently lost to the Chicago Bulls in the Eastern Conference Semifinals in six games.
In August 2011, it was announced that Alex Meruelo was buying a majority stake of the Hawks but he backed out of his intentions in November.
In December 2011, Tracy McGrady, Jerry Stackhouse, Jason Collins, Vladimir Radmanovic, Jannero Pargo, and Willie Green were signed by the Hawks.
They also picked up rookies Donald Sloan and Ivan Johnson. Sloan was waived a month later.
The Hawks finished the 2011–12 season with the fourth-best record in the Eastern Conference with 40 wins, clinching the playoffs for the fifth straight season.
However, they were eliminated by the Boston Celtics in six games in the first round.
On June 25, 2012, Danny Ferry was hired as President of Basketball Operations and General Manager.
During the 2012 NBA draft, the Hawks chose guard John Jenkins with the 23rd pick and power forward Mike Scott with the 43rd pick.
On July 2, 2012, Joe Johnson was traded to the Brooklyn Nets for Jordan Farmar, Anthony Morrow, DeShawn Stevenson, Jordan Williams, and Johan Petro, as well as a 2013 first-round pick.
That same day, Marvin Williams was traded to the Utah Jazz for point guard Devin Harris.
On July 10, 2012, Lou Williams was signed by the Hawks.
On January 21, 2013, Jannero Pargo was signed on a 10-day contract following Lou Williams' season-ending injury.

On February 21, 2013, Morrow was traded to the Dallas Mavericks for Dahntay Jones. The same day, Jeremy Tyler was acquired from Golden State Warriors in exchange for a future second-round pick, which he was waived 15 days later.
The Hawks ended the 2012–13 season with a 44–38 record, making a playoff appearance for the sixth straight season but were eliminated by the Indiana Pacers in six games in the first round.
By the end of the off-season, every player involved in the Johnson and Williams trades just a year earlier was either waived or not brought back.
The 2013 free agency period also marked the end of the Josh Smith era for Atlanta as he signed with the Detroit Pistons. Zaza Pachulia moved on to the Milwaukee Bucks.
With half the roster gone, 2012–13 proved to be a roster turnover year, paving a path to success for Mike Budenholzer.
On May 28, 2013, Mike Budenholzer was hired as the new head coach.
The Hawks entered the 2013 NBA draft with four picks and drafted Dennis Schröder (17th pick) and Shane Larkin (18th pick).
They also chose Raulzinho Neto (47th pick) and James Ennis (50th pick).
However, Larkin was traded to the Dallas Mavericks for Mike Muscala and Lucas Nogueira.
Ennis's rights were traded to the Miami Heat and Neto's to the Utah Jazz in exchange for a future second-round pick.
The Hawks brought back Kyle Korver with a four-year, $24 million deal and signed power forward Paul Millsap to a two-year, $19 million deal.
On December 26, 2013, Horford tore his right pectoral muscle and on December 30, the Hawks announced that he would undergo surgery the next day and miss the rest of the season.
The Hawks finished 38–44, their first losing season since 2008.
However, due to the weakness of the Eastern Conference, they finished as the 8th seed in the playoffs and took the top-seeded Pacers to seven games before a 92–80 loss in game 7.
On May 1, 2014, a new secondary logo was unveiled by the Hawks, which is a modernized version of the 1972–95 "Pac-Man" logo.
On July 15, 2014, Thabo Sefolosha was acquired from the Oklahoma City Thunder.
Bruce Levenson announced he would sell his share of the team on September 7, 2014 after self-reporting an inappropriate email he sent in 2012.
On January 2, 2015, it was reported that the remaining minority owners of Atlanta Hawks, LLC would join Levenson, effectively putting the entire franchise for sale.
The sale of the team as well as the operating rights to Philips Arena was handled by Goldman Sachs and Inner Circle Sports LLC.

The NBA stated that the Hawks would remain in Atlanta as a condition of their sale. Additionally, Atlanta mayor Kasim Reed stated that the city might offer incentives for a prospective owner to keep the Hawks in Atlanta for another 30 years.

On April 22, 2015, Atlanta Spirit reached a tentative agreement to sell the franchise to a group led by billionaire Tony Ressler with Grant Hill, Steven Price, Rick Schnall, Sara Blakely, Jesse Itzler, and Jami Gertz holding minority stakes. The sale was approved by the NBA Board of Governors on June 24, 2015.
On January 31, 2015, the Hawks became the first NBA team to go 17–0 in a calendar month by beating Portland.
The 2015 All-Star Game consisted of four Hawks All-Stars including Jeff Teague, Paul Millsap, Kyle Korver, and Al Horford.

On March 9, 2015, Kyle Korver and DeMarre Carroll each scored 20 points to help the Hawks become the first NBA team to 50 wins in 2014–15, scoring a season high in routing the Sacramento Kings 130–105.
The Hawks also set a franchise record by going 20-of-36 for three-pointers, breaking the mark of 19 set against the Dallas Mavericks on December 17, 1996.

On March 20, 2015, the Hawks clinched their first division title in over two decades and became the first team not based in Florida to win the NBA's Southeast Division; one week later, with a win over Miami as well as a Cleveland loss to Brooklyn, the Hawks clinched the top seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs.
The team finished a franchise-best 60–22.
In the Eastern Conference first round, the Hawks defeated the Brooklyn Nets in six games. In the Eastern Conference Semifinals, they also defeated the Washington Wizards in six games.
It was the first time they had advanced past the second round since 1967, their second-last year in St. Louis.
The Hawks advanced to the Eastern Conference Finals for the first time in franchise history but lost in four games to the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On June 22, 2016, Jeff Teague was traded to Indiana as part of a three-team deal that gave Utah's 12th pick in the 2016 NBA draft to the Hawks.
On July 8, 2016, Horford signed a four-year, $113 million contract with the Boston Celtics.
On July 13, 2017, Paul Millsap left the Hawks by signing a multi-year deal with the Denver Nuggets.
The Hawks finished the season with a 43–39 record, good enough for the fifth seed. They lost in the first round to the Washington Wizards in six games.

On June 20, 2017, Howard was traded along with the 31st overall pick in the 2017 NBA draft to the Charlotte Hornets in exchange for Marco Bellinelli, Miles Plumlee, and the 41st overall pick in the same draft. Two days later, John Collins was selected by the Hawks with the 19th overall pick.
On July 13, 2017, Paul Millsap left the Hawks by signing a multi-year deal with the Denver Nuggets.

The loss of Howard and Millsap proved insurmountable for the rebuilding Hawks as they finished with a 24–58 record in the 2017–18 season, last in the Eastern Conference, and missed the playoffs for the first time since the 2006–07 season.
On April 25, 2018, the Hawks and head coach Budenholzer mutually decided to part ways. Budenholzer later signed a deal to coach the Milwaukee Bucks.
Lloyd Pierce was hired by the Atlanta Hawks as head coach on May 11, 2018.

On June 21, the Hawks selected Luka Dončić with the third overall pick in the 2018 NBA draft and immediately traded him to the Dallas Mavericks for a 2019 protected first-round pick and the draft rights to Trae Young.
The Atlanta Hawks also selected Kevin Huerter with the 19th pick and Omari Spellman with the 30th pick of the 2018 NBA draft.
In July 2018, Jeremy Lin was acquired from the New York Knicks in a trade involving Dennis Schröder. Carmelo Anthony was also acquired but later waived through a buyout.
During the off-season, the team signed Vince Carter and Alex Len among other players.
In February 2019, Lin was bought out and eventually signed with the Toronto Raptors.
On January 23, 2020, Trae Young was selected to his first All-Star Game as a starter. He was the first Hawks player to start in an All Star Game since Dikembe Mutombo in 1998.
On February 4, 2020, Clint Capela and Nenê were acquired from the Houston Rockets
